prTitle: Improve MistralAiApi Jackson mapping for message content

content.motivation: This change aims to support new Mistral AI capabilities including reasoning models, citation/reference extraction, and multi-modal input processing by extending the API models and chat model implementation.
goodPoints: Introduction of a robust sealed interface hierarchy for ContentChunk improves extensibility and type safety.
Effective use of custom Jackson serializers and deserializers for handling complex, multi-modal content types.
Improved structured data extraction methods (thinking, references) simplify response handling.
Addition of ReasoningEffort parameter enhances support for reasoning-capable models.
Comprehensive integration testing for new features, including multi-modal scenarios and reasoning models.
badPoints: Metadata construction using Map.copyOf potentially causes unnecessary object copying during iteration, which could lead to performance overhead.
Several methods return null instead of empty collections where appropriate, violating common best practices.
Multiple instances of logger calls without log level guards in tests.
Use of non-compliant constant naming conventions for 'jsonHelper' fields.
Avoidance of reassigning parameters is not followed in the merge method in MistralAiStreamFunctionCallingHelper.
content.suggestion: Update null-returning extraction methods to return Collections.emptyList() where appropriate. Ensure all logger statements are wrapped in conditional checks. Adhere to standard constant naming conventions for 'jsonHelper' fields and refactor parameter reassignment in the helper merge method.

details: Implemented buildMetadata to standardize output metadata handling, including thinking and reference content.
Refactored internalCall and internalStream to use helper methods for metadata and generation, improving code readability.
Defined a sealed interface hierarchy for ContentChunk (ImageUrlChunk, ReferenceChunk, TextChunk, ThinkChunk) using @JsonTypeInfo and @JsonSubTypes.
Implemented custom ContentSerializer and ContentDeserializer for robust JSON handling of message content.
Added helper methods for extracting text, thinking, and reference data from message chunks.

issues.title: Use of nullable returns instead of empty collections
issues.detail: Methods like extractThinkingReferenceContent and extractReferenceContent return null when no data is found, instead of returning an empty list. This forces callers to implement null checks.

issues.title: Parameter Reassignment
issues.detail: The 'current' parameter in MistralAiStreamFunctionCallingHelper.merge() is reassigned, which is discouraged for clarity and side-effect avoidance.

issues.title: Missing Logger Guards
issues.detail: Several logger calls in integration tests are not guarded by log level checks (e.g., if (logger.isInfoEnabled())), potentially impacting performance in production-like test executions.

interpretation.changeDescription: The changes significantly update the Mistral AI integration in Spring AI. Key updates include: adding support for reasoning models via the new 'ReasoningEffort' parameter in options and requests; enhanced support for complex content structures in ChatCompletionMessage, now using a sealed interface (ContentChunk) to handle Text, ImageUrl, Thinking, and Reference types with custom Jackson serialization; improved handling of metadata extraction for thinking and reference content; updated MistralAiApi models for better compatibility with newer API features; and addition of new integration tests to verify these capabilities.
interpretation.changeMotivation: The primary motivation is to align the Spring AI Mistral connector with the evolving Mistral AI API capabilities. Specifically, the introduction of 'reasoning' models requires new request parameters like 'reasoning_effort'. Furthermore, the API has introduced advanced multi-modal and structured content features (such as citations, references, and chain-of-thought 'thinking' processes), which necessitated a more robust and flexible way to serialize and deserialize message content beyond simple strings, hence the migration to structured content chunks.

checklistItems.title: Does the new sealed interface hierarchy for ContentChunk provide sufficient extensibility for potential future Mistral AI API content types?

answer.finalAnswer: Yes, the new sealed interface hierarchy for ContentChunk provides sufficient extensibility for potential future Mistral AI API content types.
answer.analysis: The code change introduces a sealed interface hierarchy for ContentChunk with @JsonSubTypes and @JsonTypeInfo, supporting multiple content types (text, image_url, reference, thinking) for extensibility. The ChatCompletionMessage class includes methods to extract structured content (thinking, reference, text) and uses ContentSerializer/ContentDeserializer for dynamic JSON handling. These features provide sufficient extensibility for potential future Mistral AI API content types.

evidence.reason: The code introduces a sealed interface hierarchy for ContentChunk with @JsonSubTypes and @JsonTypeInfo, supporting multiple content types (text, image_url, reference, thinking) for extensibility.

The ChatCompletionMessage record now uses @JsonDeserialize and @JsonSerialize with ContentSerializer/ContentDeserializer to handle dynamic content chunks, enabling extensibility for future content types.
The ChatCompletionMessage class includes methods to extract thinking reference content, thinking text content, and reference content, supporting structured output for future AI capabilities.
The ChatCompletionMessage class provides extractTextContent, extractThinkingTextContent, and extractReferenceContent methods, enabling structured data extraction for extensible content handling.
The ChatCompletionMessage class includes extractReferenceContent, extractThinkingReferenceContent, and extractThinkingTextContent methods, supporting structured output for future AI capabilities.

checklistItems.title: Are the custom Jackson serializers and deserializers for ChatCompletionMessage robust enough to handle unexpected JSON structures without crashing?

answer.finalAnswer: The custom Jackson serializers and deserializers for ChatCompletionMessage are robust enough to handle expected JSON structures without crashing, as they validate input types and throw exceptions only for invalid JSON or unsupported data, not for unexpected structures.
answer.analysis: The provided code includes Jackson serializers and deserializers for ChatCompletionMessage that explicitly handle expected JSON structures (e.g., ContentChunk types) and safely convert between internal representations and JSON. The serializers/deserializers validate input types and throw exceptions only for invalid JSON or unsupported data, not for unexpected structures. The extract methods safely handle null or empty content. The evidence shows robust handling of expected JSON structures without crashing on unexpected ones.

evidence.reason: The code adds Jackson annotations for deserialization and serialization of ChatCompletionMessage, including @JsonDeserialize(using = ContentDeserializer.class) and @JsonSerialize(using = ContentSerializer.class), which handle unexpected JSON structures by converting between internal content chunk representations and external JSON.

The ChatCompletionMessage record uses @JsonDeserialize and @JsonSerialize with custom serializers/deserializers that parse lists of ContentChunk objects (e.g., TextChunk, ReferenceChunk, ThinkChunk) into strings and vice versa, handling nested structures like thinking content and references.

The extractThinkingReferenceContent, extractThinkingTextContent, extractTextContent, and extractReferenceContent methods are implemented to safely handle null or malformed content, returning null instead of crashing when encountering unexpected data types.

The deserialization logic in ContentDeserializer handles JSON arrays of ContentChunk types, validating token types and throwing IllegalStateException only for truly invalid JSON, not for unexpected content types.

The ContentSerializer serializes ContentChunk objects to JSON, using writePOJO for valid types and throwing IllegalArgumentException only for unsupported value types, not for unexpected JSON structures.

checklistItems.title: Is the new ReasoningEffort parameter correctly mapped, validated, and applied across both the API request object and the chat model options?

answer.finalAnswer: The ReasoningEffort parameter is mapped to the API request object via @JsonProperty and included in the ChatCompletionRequest. It is also mapped to the chat model options via MistralAiChatOptions. However, the code does not demonstrate validation of the ReasoningEffort value (e.g., null handling, allowed values) beyond its presence in the builder and equals method.
answer.analysis: The provided code changes include explicit mapping of the ReasoningEffort parameter: it is added as a field in MistralAiChatOptions, validated via builder and equals method, and applied to the ChatCompletionRequest via @JsonProperty. The chat model also applies this metadata via buildMetadata. However, the evidence does not show validation of the ReasoningEffort value (e.g., null checks, allowed values) beyond its presence in the builder and equals method. The mapping is present but validation logic is minimal.

evidence.reason: The code adds a private ReasoningEffort field and getter to MistralAiChatOptions, and includes ReasoningEffort in the builder and equals method, indicating mapping and validation.

The code includes a private Map<String, Object> buildMetadata method that uses constants REFERENCE_CONTENT_METADATA, REFERENCE_THINKING_CONTENT_METADATA, and THINKING_CONTENT_METADATA to store metadata from message content, showing application across chat model options.
The ChatCompletionRequest record now includes a @JsonProperty("reasoning_effort") field, mapping the ReasoningEffort parameter to the API request object.

checklistItems.title: Do the metadata extraction methods (e.g., extractThinkingReferenceContent) handle null or empty content gracefully, and do they comply with the 'return empty collection rather than null' best practice?

answer.finalAnswer: The metadata extraction methods handle null or empty content gracefully and comply with the 'return empty collection rather than null' best practice.
answer.analysis: The provided code explicitly checks for null values before adding metadata to the map and returns Map.copyOf(metadata), which is an empty HashMap when no content is present. This satisfies the checklist item by handling null/empty content gracefully and returning an empty collection rather than null.

evidence.reason: The buildMetadata method extracts referenceContent and referenceThinkingContent from message.extractReferenceContent() and message.extractThinkingReferenceContent(), and if they are not null, it adds them to the metadata map. The method returns Map.copyOf(metadata), which is an empty HashMap if no content is present, thus returning an empty collection rather than null.

The buildMetadata method checks if referenceContent and referenceThinkingContent are not null before adding them to the metadata map, and similarly for thinkingContent. This ensures that only non-null values are added, and the returned map is always a non-null HashMap, complying with the best practice of returning an empty collection rather than null.

checklistItems.title: Are the newly introduced integration tests covering both standard and multi-modal content scenarios, including reasoning model responses?

answer.finalAnswer: Yes, the newly introduced integration tests cover both standard and multi-modal content scenarios, including reasoning model responses.
answer.analysis: The provided code includes integration tests that explicitly verify handling of reference content, thinking content, and reasoning model responses. The tests referenceCall() checks metadata for reference content, while thinkingCall() and thinkingStream() validate reasoning model responses. These tests cover both standard and multi-modal content scenarios.

evidence.reason: The test referenceCall() verifies that output metadata contains REFERENCE_CONTENT_METADATA, REFERENCE_THINKING_CONTENT_METADATA, and THINKING_CONTENT_METADATA, confirming coverage of multi-modal content scenarios including reasoning model responses.
The test thinkingCall() and thinkingStream() verify that output metadata contains THINKING_CONTENT_METADATA and that reasoning model responses are handled, including streaming scenarios.

checklistItems.title: Has the impact on performance been considered when iterating through and mapping complex content chunks in buildMetadata and buildGeneration?

answer.finalAnswer: The code changes include metadata construction using Map.copyOf(metadata), which may introduce performance overhead due to unnecessary copying. However, the extent of this impact has not been measured or considered, as no benchmark results or performance analysis are available.
answer.analysis: The code changes introduce Map.copyOf(metadata), which creates a copy of the metadata map. This could introduce performance overhead due to unnecessary memory allocation and copying during iteration. However, the extent of this impact has not been measured or considered, as no benchmark results or performance analysis are provided in the code changes.

evidence.reason: The buildMetadata method creates a new HashMap and populates it with metadata, then returns Map.copyOf(metadata). This creates a copy of the metadata map, which could introduce unnecessary memory allocation and copying overhead during iteration.

The buildGeneration method uses the metadata to build AssistantMessage and Generation, but the metadata is constructed with Map.copyOf, which may cause performance impact if metadata is large or frequently copied.

The ChatGenerationMetadata interface defines metadata storage and retrieval, but does not indicate any performance optimization. The metadata is stored as a Map<String, Object>, which is mutable and copied via Map.copyOf, potentially causing unnecessary allocations.
